newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian jet makes emergency landing in Vladivostok.
newsitem.headline: Russian jet makes emergency landing in Vladivostok.

text.p: A passenger jet operated by Russian private carrier Orient-Avia made an emergency landing at Vladivostok international airport in the Russian Far East on Friday after an engine quit in flight, a company official said.

"The Ilyushin-62M jet which operates regularly between Moscow and Vladivostok had problems with one of its four engines," Orient-Avia's flight service official told Reuters, adding that the engine had stopped running in flight.
He said the landing was successfull and no one was hurt. He did not say how many people were on the plane, which has a passenger capacity of 183 people.
"We do not have details of this incident yet," the official said.
The Russian Air Traffic centre in Moscow confirmed that the Il-62M had had engine problems during its flight.

Moscow-based Orient-Avia was established in 1994. It operates four Ilyushin-62M jets on regular long-range routes between Moscow and Vladivostok and Petropavlovsk-Kamchatsky in the Russian Far East and from Vladivostok to Bangkok, Thailand.
The company's two Tupolev-134 short range planes serve short domestic routes.
